title: Ear Train: choose a new visual identity
question: Compare the same M2 Practice and Insights content on desktop and mobile. These are generated concept mockups, not implemented screens; analytics values are illustrative. Choose, revise, or explore another hand.

options.label: Phrase Desk
options.thesis: A steady working baseline makes listening the subject and evidence easy to inspect.
options.viewport: Chord and answers share an editorial baseline; Insights stacks outcome, evidence and the next action.
options.risk: Can feel like a specialist editor; labels and touch controls must stay immediately familiar.

raised.raise: Use uncompromising text contrast and tabular evidence without visual noise.
Give the current listening task exclusive focal priority without swipe navigation.
Keep one disciplined identity across quiet practice and dense evidence.
Keep session position and recorded outcomes legible without invented stamps or steps.
Bind each qualification and action visibly to the evidence it belongs to.

options.label: Ensemble Score
options.lineage: Readable contemporary ensemble parts and rehearsal marks
options.thesis: A clear musical anchor sits above a measured, unchanging response grid.
options.viewport: A spacious chord anchor and measured answer rows; Insights uses aligned evidence bands with nearby practice actions.
options.risk: Closest to familiar musician tools; discipline must avoid decorative staves or a generic blue dashboard.

options.label: Signal Route
options.lineage: International terminal wayfinding translated into a listening tool
options.thesis: One unmistakable destination and action at every decision point.
options.viewport: A restrained yellow task band anchors the chord; answer keys and evidence remain on white, with edge-aligned actions.
options.case: Stronger immediate wayfinding; weaker musician identification than the grounded workspaces.
options.risk: Yellow can become visually tiring; reserve it for task location and the main action, never the entire page.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: Black/white lattices and mono data columns
options.thesis: Black/white lattices and mono data columns
options.viewport: Chord, answers and evidence as a monochrome scan field.
options.case: After translation it remains less musically recognizable and more cognitively dense than Phrase Desk.
options.risk: Dense plots would compete with listening; no strobing or fake audio visualization.

options.label: Single-Item Feed
options.viewport: One question per viewport, with secondary actions at the edge.
options.case: The single-item focus is useful, but media chrome is less recognizable and snap navigation conflicts with the approved progression.
options.kept: Exclusive focal priority without swipe navigation.
options.risk: Must not introduce swipe-to-next, hidden degree choices or media-first content.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.viewport: A catalog-like practice entry and evidence index.
options.case: Music culture resonates, but coded labels, tiny metadata and a plot-dominated field weaken both task recognition and usable clarity.
options.kept: Consistent identity across sparse and dense views.
options.risk: Color codes cannot replace degree labels or outcome text.

options.label: Session Coupon
options.viewport: Session positions and responses occupy fixed ruled fields.
options.case: Even without literal airline content, the travel ritual is less musician-specific and adds field scanning to a simple listening task.
options.kept: Persistent session position and recorded outcomes.
options.risk: No tear-off progression, fake validation stamps or compulsory steps.

options.label: Reference Rail
options.lineage: Two-column reference setting with an annotation rail
options.thesis: Two-column reference setting with an annotation rail
options.viewport: Evidence and its qualifications align around a narrow central rail.
options.case: Readable at reference scale, but dense apparatus is less familiar during ear practice and introduces more scanning than Phrase Desk.
options.kept: Keep qualifications and actions next to their evidence.
options.risk: Small apparatus and overlapping margins are unsuitable for phone practice.

canonCard.label: Familiar Workspace
canonCard.thesis: The conventional training app, executed with clear native controls and minimal chrome.
canonCard.viewport: Compact top navigation, centered practice grid and a straightforward stacked Insights overview.
canonCard.risk: Lowest visual learning cost, but intentionally less distinctive.
